content.title: Recommendations for the management of anaemia and iron deficiency in patients with heart failure

recommendations.recommendation: It is recommended that all patients with HF be periodically screened for anaemia and iron deficiency with a full blood count, serum ferritin concentration, and TSAT.
recommendations.intended_outcome: Periodic screening to detect anaemia and iron deficiency

recommendations.recommendation: Intravenous iron supplementation with ferric carboxymaltose should be considered in symptomatic patients with LVEF <45% and iron deficiency, defined as serum ferritin <100 ng/mL or serum ferritin 100–299 ng/mL with TSAT <20%, to alleviate HF symptoms, improve exercise capacity and QOL.
recommendations.population: Symptomatic heart failure patients with LVEF <45% and iron deficiency
recommendations.iron_deficiency_definition: serum ferritin <100 ng/mL OR serum ferritin 100–299 ng/mL with TSAT <20%
recommendations.intended_outcome: Alleviate HF symptoms, improve exercise capacity and quality of life

recommendations.recommendation: Intravenous iron supplementation with ferric carboxymaltose should be considered in symptomatic HF patients recently hospitalized for HF and with LVEF <50% and iron deficiency, defined as serum ferritin <100 ng/mL or serum ferritin 100–299 ng/mL with TSAT <20%, to reduce the risk of HF hospitalization.
recommendations.population: Symptomatic HF patients recently hospitalized for HF with LVEF <50% and iron deficiency
recommendations.iron_deficiency_definition: serum ferritin <100 ng/mL OR serum ferritin 100–299 ng/mL with TSAT <20%
recommendations.intended_outcome: Reduce risk of heart failure hospitalization
